system.name: Contract Shadow Logic
system.one_liner: a formal RTL verification technique that scales secure-speculation contract checking to out-of-order processors

components.name: ISA1
components.role: single-cycle reference machine running program P with one secret memory instance

components.name: ISA2
components.role: single-cycle reference machine running program P with a differing secret memory instance

components.name: 1-cycle Processor
components.role: single-cycle ISA-level machine used to define the contract constraint check

components.name: Contract Constraint Check
components.role: equivalence check on O_ISA deciding whether program P must be protected

components.name: All Programs
components.role: the universe of programs filtered by the contract constraint check

components.name: OoO1
components.role: out-of-order processor instance with a secret memory instance

components.name: OoO2
components.role: out-of-order processor instance with a differing secret memory instance

components.name: IF
components.role: instruction fetch stage of the out-of-order pipeline

components.name: ID
components.role: instruction decode stage of the out-of-order pipeline

components.name: ROB
components.role: reorder buffer stage of the out-of-order pipeline

components.name: Commit
components.role: commit stage of the out-of-order pipeline

components.name: MEM
components.role: memory unit of the out-of-order processor

components.name: Leakage Assertion Check
components.role: equivalence check on O_muArch deciding whether the microarchitecture leaks the secret

flows.what: O_ISA computed directly on the out-of-order machine via shadow logic

content.key_idea: Fold the ISA-level contract constraint check into shadow logic attached to the out-of-order processors, reducing a four-machine verification problem to two machines plus shadow logic.
content.reading_order: Left panel (a) baseline read top-to-bottom then right; the black arrow leads to panel (b) which mirrors the OoO boxes with the ISA check now embedded via shadow logic.

summary: This two-panel figure from the Contract Shadow Logic paper contrasts a baseline RTL security-verification scheme (a) with the proposed technique (b). In the baseline, two single-cycle processors running the same program under differing secret memories feed a Contract Constraint Check producing an ISA-level observation O_ISA, while two out-of-order processors — each with IF, ID, ROB, FU, MEM and Commit stages — feed a Leakage Assertion Check producing a microarchitectural observation O_muArch, together requiring four state machines. Panel (b) shows the contract constraint check folded directly into shadow logic attached to the two out-of-order processors, cutting the verification problem to two machines plus lightweight shadow logic. Boxes are plain white rectangles with thin black outlines; colored dashed (green) and dotted (blue) lines distinguish the ISA-level and microarchitecture-level equivalence-check signals, and small icons (funnel, magnifying glass, pickaxe) annotate the filtering, checking, and newly-added logic.
summary_zh: 图1对比了基线验证方案(a)与Contract Shadow Logic方案(b)：基线用四台状态机分别做ISA级契约约束检查和乱序处理器泄漏断言检查；新方案把约束检查以影子逻辑直接嵌入乱序处理器，将四机问题降为两机加影子逻辑，绿色虚线与蓝色点线区分两类等价性检查信号。
notes: The pipeline stage boxes (IF/ID/ROB/FU/MEM/Commit) are standard out-of-order microarchitecture labels not individually explained in the excerpted text; their roles are inferred from general architecture convention plus the figure.
